translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day a great amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月乙亥，割揚州吳郡置吳州，割錢塘縣為郡，屬焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, yihai day, Yangzhou's Wu commandery was split to establish Wu prefecture; Qiantang county was split as a commandery and attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter on yihai day Yangzhou's Wu commandery was split to establish Wu prefecture; Qiantang county was made a commandery and attached.

sentences.zh: 景子，以蕭巖為平東將軍、開府儀同三司、東揚州刺史，蕭瓛為安東將軍、吳州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengzi day Yan was made Pacify East General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of East Yangzhou; Xuan was made Pacify East General and Inspector of Wu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Yan was made pacify east general, opener equal to the three dukes, and East Yangzhou inspector; Xuan was made pacify east general and Wu prefecture inspector.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司豫章王叔英兼司徒。

translations.literal: On dinghai day Grand General of Agile Cavalry, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Prince of Yuzhang Shuying, was concurrently made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Shuying, Prince of Yuzhang, grand general of agile cavalry and opener equal to the three dukes, was concurrently made minister of education.

sentences.zh: 十二月景辰，以前鎮衛將軍、開府儀同三司、東揚州刺史鄱陽王伯山為鎮衛大將軍、開府儀同三司，[21]前中衛將軍晉安王伯恭為中衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, gengchen day, the former General Who Garrisons the Guard, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, Prince of Poyang Boshan, was made Grand General Who Garrisons the Guard, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Editorial footnote marker 21. the former Grand General of the Central Guard, Prince of Jin'an Bogong, was made Grand General of the Central Guard and Right Grand Master of the Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month on gengchen day Boshan, Prince of Poyang, former general who garrisons the guard, opener equal to the three dukes, and East Yangzhou inspector, was made grand general who garrisons the guard with a mansion equal to the three dukes [21]; Bogong, Prince of Jin'an, former grand general of the central guard, was made grand general of the central guard and right grand master of the glory.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛巳，立皇子恮為東陽王，恬為錢塘王。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, xinsi day, the prince Quan was established as Prince of Dongyang; Tian as Prince of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of year 2 on xinsi day Prince Quan was made Prince of Dongyang; Tian Prince of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣散騎常侍周羅睺帥兵屯峽口。

translations.literal: That month Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant Zhou Luohou led troops to garrison at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhou Luohou, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, led troops to garrison Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊申，有群鼠無數，自〔蔡〕洲岸入石頭渡淮，[22]至于青塘兩岸，數日死，隨流出江。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, wushen day, a swarm of rats without number from [Cai] Isle's shore entered Shitou, crossed the ford on the Huai, Editorial footnote marker 22. reaching both banks of Qingtang; after several days they died and flowed out with the current into the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer on wushen day countless rats from Cai Isle's shore entered Shitou, crossed the Huai ford [22], reaching both banks of Qingtang; after several days they died and flowed out into the river.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書蔡徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Minister of the Left Household Cai Zheng was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Cai Zheng of the left household ministry was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 是月，郢州南浦水黑如墨。

translations.literal: That month the Nanpu water of Yingzhou was black as ink.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Nanpu water of Yingzhou was black as ink.

sentences.zh: 五月壬午，以安前將軍廬陵王伯仁為特進。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, renyang day, General Who Secures the Van, Prince of Luling Boren, was made special grand master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month on renyang day Boren, Prince of Luling, general who secures the van, was made special grand master.

sentences.zh: 甲午，東冶鑄鐵，有物赤色如數斗，[23]自天墜鎔所，有聲隆隆如雷，鐵飛出牆外燒民家。

translations.literal: On jiawu day in the eastern foundry iron was cast; there was a thing red as several dou, Editorial footnote marker 23. falling from heaven into the smelting place, with a sound rumbling like thunder; iron flew outside the wall and burned people's houses.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the eastern foundry iron was cast; a thing red as several dou [23] fell from heaven into the smelter, rumbling like thunder; iron flew outside the wall and burned houses.

sentences.zh: 六月戊戌，扶南國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, wuxu day, the state of Funan sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month on wuxu day Funan sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚子，廢皇太子胤為吳興王，立軍師將軍、揚州刺史始安王深為皇太子。

translations.literal: On gengzi day the crown prince Yin was deposed as Prince of Wuxing; the Military Adviser General and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince of Shian Shen, was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Crown Prince Yin was deposed as Prince of Wuxing; Shen, Prince of Shian, military adviser general and Yangzhou inspector, was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，平南將軍、江州刺史南平王嶷進號鎮南將軍；

translations.literal: On xinchou day Pacify South General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, Prince of Nanping Yan, was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons South;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Yan, Prince of Nanping, pacify south general and Jiangzhou inspector, was promoted to general who garrisons south;

sentences.zh: 忠武將軍、南徐州刺史永嘉王彥進號安北將軍；

translations.literal: Loyal Martial General and Inspector of South Xuzhou, Prince of Yongjia Yan, was advanced in title to General Who Secures the North;
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Prince of Yongjia, loyal martial general and South Xuzhou inspector, was promoted to general who secures the north;

sentences.zh: 會稽王莊為翊前將軍、揚州刺史；

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Zhuang was made Aide-before-the-Throne General and Inspector of Yangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang, Prince of Kuaiji, was made aide-before-the-throne general and Yangzhou inspector;

sentences.zh: 宣惠將軍、尚書令江總進號中權將軍；

translations.literal: Manifest Grace General and Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zong was advanced in title to Central Authority General;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong, manifest grace general and director of the Masters of Writing, was promoted to central authority general;

sentences.zh: 雲麾將軍、太子詹事袁憲為尚書僕射；

translations.literal: Cloud Banner General and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Yuan Xian was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian, cloud banner general and junior tutor of the heir apparent, was made vice minister;

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射謝伷為特進；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie You was made special grand master;
translations.idiomatic: Xie You, vice minister, was made special grand master;

sentences.zh: 寧遠將軍、新除吏部尚書蔡徵進號安右將軍。

translations.literal: General of Far Pacification and newly appointed Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng was advanced in title to Secure-the-Right General.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zheng, general of far pacification and newly minister of personnel, was promoted to secure-the-right general.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以安右將軍魯廣達為中領軍。

translations.literal: On jiachen day Secure-the-Right General Lu Guangda was made Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Lu Guangda, secure-the-right general, was made central army commander.

sentences.zh: [24]丁巳，大風至自西北激濤水入石頭城，淮渚暴溢，漂沒舟乘。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 24. On dingsi day a great wind came from the northwest and drove the surging waters into Shitou city; the Huai's islets overflowed violently and boats were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 24. On dingsi day a great wind came from the northwest and drove surging water into Shitou; the Huai's islets overflowed and boats were drowned.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己亥，立皇子蕃為吳郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, jihai day, the prince Fan was established as Prince of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter on jihai day Prince Fan was made Prince of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以度支尚書、領大著作姚察為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On xinchou day Minister of Revenue and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Yao Cha was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Yao Cha, minister of revenue and recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 己酉，輿駕幸莫府山，大校獵。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the imperial carriage visited Mofu Mountain and held a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day the emperor visited Mofu Mountain and held a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁卯，詔曰：「夫議獄緩刑，皇王之所垂範，勝殘去殺，仁人之所用心。

translations.literal: On dingmao day an edict said: "To deliberate on punishments and slow executions is what emperors and kings hand down as model; to overcome cruelty and remove killing is what humane men apply their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict said: "To deliberate on punishments and slow executions is what emperors and kings hand down as model; to overcome cruelty and remove killing is what humane men apply their hearts.

sentences.zh: 自畫冠既息，刻吏斯起，法令滋章，手足無措。

translations.literal: Since the painted cap ceased, the carving clerk arose; laws and orders grow daily and hands and feet have nowhere to place.
translations.idiomatic: Since the painted cap ceased, the carving clerk arose; laws grow daily and hands and feet have nowhere to place.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨區宇，屬當澆末，輕重之典，在政未康，小大之情，興言多愧。

translations.literal: We face the realm in a time that is thin and shallow; the canon of light and heavy is not yet at peace in government; in small and great feeling We speak with much shame.
translations.idiomatic: We face the realm in a thin age; the canon of light and heavy is not yet at peace; in small and great feeling We speak with much shame.

sentences.zh: 眷茲狴犴，有軫哀矜，可克日於大政殿訊獄。

translations.literal: Looking on these prisons, Our breast is moved to pity; on a set day in the Great Governance Hall trials may be held.
translations.idiomatic: Looking on these prisons, Our breast is moved to pity; on a set day trials may be held in the Great Governance Hall.

sentences.zh: 」壬申，以鎮南將軍、江州刺史南平王嶷為征西將軍、郢州刺史，安北將軍、南徐州刺史永嘉王彥為安南將軍、江州刺史，軍師將軍南海王虔為安北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: " On renshen day General Who Garrisons South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, Prince of Nanping Yan, was made General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Yingzhou; General Who Secures the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou, Prince of Yongjia Yan, was made General Who Pacifies South and Inspector of Jiangzhou; Military Adviser General, Prince of Nanhai Qian, was made General Who Secures the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Yan, Prince of Nanping, general who garrisons south and Jiangzhou inspector, was made general who campaigns west and Yingzhou inspector; Yan, Prince of Yongjia, general who secures the north and South Xuzhou inspector, was made general who pacifies south and Jiangzhou inspector; Qian, Prince of Nanhai, military adviser general, was made general who secures the north and South Xuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: [25]景子，立皇弟叔榮為新昌王，叔匡為太原王。

translations.literal: On jingzi day [25] the emperor's younger brother Shurong was made Prince of Xinchang and Shukuang Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jingzi day [25] the emperor's younger brother Shurong was made prince of Xinchang and Shukuang prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 是月，隋遣晉王廣眾軍來伐，自巴、蜀、沔、漢下流至廣陵，數十道俱入，緣江鎮戍，相繼奏聞。

translations.literal: That month Sui sent Prince of Jin Guang with a host of armies to attack; from Ba, Shu, Mian, and Han they came downriver to Guangling; several tens of routes entered together, and the garrisons along the Yangtze reported in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That month Sui sent the Prince of Jin, Guang, at the head of many armies to attack; from Ba, Shu, the Mian, and the Han they descended to Guangling along several dozen routes at once, and river garrisons reported one after another.

sentences.zh: 時新除湘州刺史施文慶、中書舍人沈客卿掌機密用事，並抑而不言，故無備禦。

translations.literal: At that time the newly appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou Shi Wenqing and Secretariat Attendant Shen Keqing held confidential power; both suppressed the reports and did not speak, so there was no defense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the newly appointed Xiangzhou inspector Shi Wenqing and secretariat attendant Shen Keqing held confidential power; both suppressed the reports and said nothing, so the court was unprepared.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月乙丑朔，霧氣四塞。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of year 3, on yichou the new moon, mist filled on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of year 3, on yichou the new moon, mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 是日，隋總管賀若弼自北道廣陵濟京口，總管韓擒虎趨橫江，[26]濟採石，自南道將會弼軍。

translations.literal: That day Sui Inspector-General He Ruo Bi from the northern route crossed from Guangling to Jingkou; Inspector-General Han Qin Hu pressed toward Hengjiang, [26] crossed Caishi, and from the southern route was to join Bi's army.
translations.idiomatic: That day Sui inspector-general He Ruo Bi from the northern route crossed from Guangling to Jingkou; inspector-general Han Qin Hu pressed toward Hengjiang, [26] crossed Caishi, and from the south was to join Bi's army.

sentences.zh: 景寅，採石戍主徐子建馳啟告變。

translations.literal: On yinyin day the Caishi garrison commander Xu Zijian galloped in with urgent news of the change.
translations.idiomatic: On yinyin day Caishi garrison commander Xu Zijian galloped in with urgent news.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，召公卿入議軍旅。

translations.literal: On dingmao day the emperor summoned the high ministers to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the emperor summoned the high ministers to discuss military affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，內外戒嚴，以驃騎將軍蕭摩訶、[27]護軍將軍樊毅、中領軍魯廣達並為都督，遣南豫州刺史樊猛帥舟師出白下，散騎常侍皋文奏將兵鎮南豫州。

translations.literal: On wuchen day inner and outer defenses were ordered; Cavalry General Xiao Mohe, [27] Protector of the Army Fan Yi, and Central Army Commander Lu Guangda were all made commanders; Southern Yuzhou Inspector Fan Meng was sent to lead the fleet out from Baixia; Regular Attendant Gao Wenzou was to lead troops and garrison Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day inner and outer defenses were ordered; cavalry general Xiao Mohe, [27] protector of the army Fan Yi, and central army commander Lu Guangda were all made commanders; Southern Yuzhou inspector Fan Meng led the fleet out from Baixia; regular attendant Gao Wenzou was to lead troops and garrison Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賀若弼攻陷南徐州。

translations.literal: On gengwu day He Ruo Bi stormed and took Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day He Ruo Bi stormed and took Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，韓擒虎又陷南豫州，文奏敗還。

translations.literal: On xinwei day Han Qin Hu again took Southern Yuzhou; Wenzou was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Han Qin Hu again took Southern Yuzhou; Wenzou was defeated and returned.

sentences.zh: 至是隋軍南北道並進。

translations.literal: By then the Sui armies on north and south routes were advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Sui armies on north and south routes were advancing together.

sentences.zh: 後主遣驃騎大將軍、司徒豫章王叔英屯朝

translations.literal: Houzhu sent Cavalry Grand General and Minister of Works Prince of Yuzhang Shuying to garrison Chao
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu sent cavalry grand general and minister of works Shuying, Prince of Yuzhang, to garrison Chao

translations.literal: (shi)
translations.idiomatic: (shi)

sentences.zh: 〔堂〕，[28]蕭摩訶屯樂遊苑，樊毅屯耆闍寺，魯廣達屯白土岡，忠武將軍孔範屯寶田寺。

translations.literal: [tang], [28] Xiao Mohe garrisoned the Pleasure Gardens, Fan Yi the Jataka Temple, Lu Guangda White Earth Mound, and Loyal-and-Martial General Kong Fan the Baotian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: [tang], [28] Xiao Mohe garrisoned the Pleasure Gardens, Fan Yi the Jataka Temple, Lu Guangda White Earth Mound, and loyal-and-martial general Kong Fan the Baotian Temple.

sentences.zh: 己卯，鎮東大將軍任忠自吳興入赴，仍屯朱雀門。

translations.literal: On jimao day Pacify-the-East Grand General Ren Zhong came in from Wuxing and still garrisoned the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day pacify-the-east grand general Ren Zhong came in from Wuxing and still garrisoned the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賀若弼進據鍾山，頓白土岡之東南。

translations.literal: On xinsi day He Ruo Bi advanced and held Bell Mountain, encamped southeast of White Earth Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day He Ruo Bi advanced and held Bell Mountain, encamped southeast of White Earth Mound.

sentences.zh: 甲申，後主遣眾軍與弼合戰，眾軍敗績。

translations.literal: On jiashen day Houzhu sent the mass of armies to join battle with Bi; the armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Houzhu sent the mass of armies to join battle with Bi; the armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 弼乘勝至樂遊苑，魯廣達猶督散兵力戰，不能拒。

translations.literal: Bi pressed the victory to the Pleasure Gardens; Lu Guangda still directed scattered troops in fierce fighting but could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Bi pressed the victory to the Pleasure Gardens; Lu Guangda still directed scattered troops in fierce fighting but could not resist.

sentences.zh: 弼進攻宮城，燒北掖門。

translations.literal: Bi attacked the palace city and burned the North Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bi attacked the palace city and burned the North Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 是時韓擒虎率眾自新林至于石子岡，任忠出降於擒虎，仍引擒虎經朱雀航趣宮城，自南掖門而入。

translations.literal: At that time Han Qin Hu led his host from Xinlin to Shizi Mound; Ren Zhong went out and surrendered to Qin Hu, then led Qin Hu by the Vermilion Bird crossing toward the palace city and entered by the South Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Qin Hu led his host from Xinlin to Shizi Mound; Ren Zhong went out and surrendered to Qin Hu, then led Qin Hu by the Vermilion Bird crossing toward the palace city and entered by the South Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 於是城內文武百司皆遁出，唯尚書僕射袁憲在殿內。

translations.literal: Then the civil and military hundred offices within the city all fled out; only Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Xian remained in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Then the civil and military hundred offices within the city all fled; only vice director of the masters of writing Yuan Xian remained in the hall.

sentences.zh: 尚書令江總、吏部尚書姚察、度支尚書袁權、前度支尚書王瑗、侍中王寬居省中。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Zong, Minister of Personnel Yao Cha, Minister of Revenue Yuan Quan, former Minister of Revenue Wang Yuan, and Palace Attendant Wang Kuan stayed in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the masters of writing Jiang Zong, minister of personnel Yao Cha, minister of revenue Yuan Quan, former minister of revenue Wang Yuan, and palace attendant Wang Kuan stayed in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後主聞兵至，從宮人十餘出後堂景陽殿，將自投于井，袁憲侍側，苦諫不從，後閤舍人夏侯公韻又以身蔽井，後主與爭久之，方得入焉。

translations.literal: When Houzhu heard the army had come, he went out from the rear hall Jingyang Pavilion with a dozen palace women and was about to throw himself into a well; Yuan Xian attended at his side and bitterly remonstrated but he would not listen; Rear-Gate Attendant Xia Hou Gongyun again covered the well with his body; Houzhu struggled with him a long time before he could enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu heard the army had come, he went out from the rear-hall Jingyang Pavilion with a dozen palace women and was about to throw himself into a well; Yuan Xian at his side bitterly remonstrated but he would not listen; rear-gate attendant Xia Hou Gongyun again covered the well with his body; Houzhu struggled with him a long time before he could enter.

sentences.zh: 及夜，為隋軍所執。

translations.literal: By night he was seized by the Sui army.
translations.idiomatic: By night he was seized by the Sui army.

sentences.zh: 景戌，晉王廣入據京城。

translations.literal: On jingxu day Prince of Jin Guang entered and held the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jingxu day the Prince of Jin, Guang, entered and held the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月己巳，後主與王公百司發自建鄴，入于長安。

translations.literal: On jisi day of the third month Houzhu with the kings, dukes, and hundred offices set out from Jiankang and entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day of the third month Houzhu with the kings, dukes, and hundred offices set out from Jiankang and entered Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽四年十一月壬子，薨於洛陽，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Renshou year 4 of Sui, on renzi day, he died at Luoyang, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Sui Renshou year 4, on renzi day, he died at Luoyang, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 追贈大將軍，封長城縣公，謚曰煬，葬河南洛陽之芒山。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of the Chief Wall county; his posthumous title was Yang; he was buried on Mang Mountain in Henan, Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given grand general and enfeoffed as duke of Chief Wall county; his posthumous title was Yang; he was buried on Mang Mountain at Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 史臣侍中鄭國公魏徵曰：

translations.literal: The historian, Palace Attendant and Duke of Zheng Wei Zheng, said:
translations.idiomatic: The historian, palace attendant and Duke of Zheng Wei Zheng, said:

sentences.zh: 高祖拔起壟畝，有雄桀之姿。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor rose from the furrow with a heroic mettle.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor rose from the furrow with heroic mettle.

sentences.zh: 始佐下藩，奮英奇之略，弭節南海，職思靜亂。

translations.literal: At first he aided a lower fief and deployed singular strategy; he held his staff in the southern sea with the charge to still disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At first he aided a lower fief and deployed singular strategy; he held his staff in the southern sea charged to still disorder.

sentences.zh: 援旗北邁，義在勤王，掃侯景於既成，拯梁室於已墜。

translations.literal: He raised his banner northward with the righteousness of aiding the throne, swept Hou Jing when already formed, and rescued the Liang house when already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his banner northward in righteousness to aid the throne, swept Hou Jing when already formed, and rescued the Liang house when already fallen.

sentences.zh: 天網絕而復續，國步屯而更康，百神有主，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Heaven's net, broken, was joined again; the state's step, halted, grew tranquil again; the hundred spirits had a lord and the old realm was not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's net, broken, was joined again; the state's step, halted, grew tranquil again; the hundred spirits had a lord and the old realm was not lost.

sentences.zh: 魏王之延漢鼎祚，宋武之反晉乘輿，懋績鴻勳，無以尚也。

translations.literal: The King of Wei's prolonging the Han tripod and Song Wu's turning back the Jin imperial carriage—such great deeds and splendid merit have nothing above them.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei's prolonging the Han tripod and Song Wu's turning back the Jin imperial carriage—such great deeds and splendid merit have nothing above them.

sentences.zh: 于時內難未弭，外鄰勍敵，王琳作梗於上流，周、齊搖蕩於江、漢，畏首畏尾，若存若亡，此之不圖，遽移天歷，雖皇靈有睠，何其速也？

translations.literal: At that time inner strife was not yet stilled and outer neighbors were fierce foes; Wang Lin made obstruction on the upper reaches and Zhou and Qi shook the Jiang and Han—fearing head and tail as if existing yet not existing—to shift the heavenly mandate without planning this, though the imperial numen had regard, how swift it was!
translations.idiomatic: At that time inner strife was not yet stilled and outer neighbors were fierce foes; Wang Lin made obstruction on the upper reaches and Zhou and Qi shook the Jiang and Han—fearing head and tail as if existing yet not existing—to shift the heavenly mandate without planning this, though the imperial numen had regard, how swift it was!

sentences.zh: 然志度弘遠，懷抱豁如，或取士於仇讎，或擢才於亡命，掩其受金之過，宥其吠堯之罪，委以心腹爪牙，咸能得其死力，故乃決機百勝，成此三分，方諸鼎峙之雄，足以無慚權、備矣。

translations.literal: Yet his will and measure were broad and far, his breast open as if level; he took men from among foes and raised talent from among fugitives, covered their taking-gold faults and pardoned their barking-at-Yao crimes, entrusted them as heart, belly, claws, and teeth, and all could give him their utmost strength—thus he decided the hundred battles and formed this tripartite realm; compared with the heroes of the tripod age he need not blush before Cao and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his will and measure were broad and far, his breast open as if level; he took men from among foes and raised talent from among fugitives, covered their taking-gold faults and pardoned their barking-at-Yao crimes, entrusted them as heart, belly, claws, and teeth, and all could give him their utmost strength—thus he decided the hundred battles and formed this tripartite realm; compared with the heroes of the tripod age he need not blush before Cao and Liu.

sentences.zh: 世祖天姿叡哲，清明在躬，早預經綸，知民疾苦，思擇令典，庶幾至治。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen by nature was wise and penetrating, with clarity in his person; early he took part in ordering the realm and knew the people's hardship; he thought to choose good statutes and nearly reach supreme order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen by nature was wise and penetrating, with clarity in his person; early he took part in ordering the realm and knew the people's hardship; he thought to choose good statutes and nearly reach supreme order.

sentences.zh: 德刑並用，戡濟艱虞，群凶授首，彊鄰震懾。

translations.literal: Virtue and punishments were used together; he cut through hard times, the fierce all offered their heads, and strong neighbors were shaken in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue and punishments were used together; he cut through hard times, the fierce all offered their heads, and strong neighbors were shaken in awe.

sentences.zh: 雖忠厚之化未能及遠，恭儉之風足以垂訓，若不尚明察，則守文之良主也。

translations.literal: Though the transformation of generous loyalty did not reach far, the wind of respectful frugality was enough to leave instruction; had he not prized sharp discernment, he would have been a good lord who kept the written rule.
translations.idiomatic: Though the transformation of generous loyalty did not reach far, the wind of respectful frugality was enough to leave instruction; had he not prized sharp discernment, he would have been a good lord who kept the written rule.

sentences.zh: 臨川年長於成王，過微於太甲。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was older than the Duke of Zhou of Cheng's time and went too far beyond the Duke of Taijia.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor was older than the Duke of Zhou of Cheng's time and went too far beyond the Duke of Taijia.

sentences.zh: 宣帝有周公之親，無伊尹之志，明辟不復，桐宮遂往，欲加之罪，其無辭乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan had the Duke of Zhou's kinship but not the Duke of Yin's intent; the enlightened ruler did not return, and the Tung Palace went on—wishing to add guilt to him, was there no plea?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had the Duke of Zhou's kinship but not the Duke of Yin's intent; the enlightened ruler did not return, and the Tung Palace went on—wishing to add guilt to him, was there no plea?

sentences.zh: 高宗爰自在田，雅量宏廓，登庸御極，民歸其厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, from the time he was in the fields, had a generous measure and broad forbearance; ascending to rule the summit, the people returned to his depth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, from the time he was in the fields, had a generous measure and broad forbearance; ascending to rule the summit, the people returned to his depth.

sentences.zh: 惠以使下，[29]寬以容眾。

translations.literal: He was kind in employing those below, [29] and broad in containing the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was kind in employing those below, [29] and broad in containing the multitude.

sentences.zh: 智勇爭奮，師出有名，揚旆分麾，風行電掃，辟土千里，奄有淮、泗，戰勝攻取之勢，近古未之有也。

translations.literal: Wisdom and courage vied in ardor; the army went out with a righteous name; banners were raised and commands divided—the wind moved and lightning swept; a thousand li of territory was opened and Huai and Si were suddenly held—the momentum of victory in attack in recent antiquity had never been its like.
translations.idiomatic: Wisdom and courage vied in ardor; the army went out with a righteous name; banners were raised and commands divided—the wind moved and lightning swept; a thousand li of territory was opened and Huai and Si were suddenly held—the momentum of victory in attack in recent antiquity had never been its like.

sentences.zh: [30]既而君侈民勞，將驕卒墮，帑藏空竭，折衄師徒，於是秦人方彊，遂窺兵於江上矣。

translations.literal: [30] Afterward the lord was extravagant and the people weary; generals were proud and soldiers slack; the treasury was empty and the army was broken—then the Qin people grew strong and looked with troops upon the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: [30] Afterward the lord was extravagant and the people weary; generals were proud and soldiers slack; the treasury was empty and the army was broken—then the Qin people grew strong and looked with troops upon the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 李克以為吳之先亡，由乎數戰〔數勝〕，[31]數戰則民疲，數勝則主驕，以驕主御疲民，未有不亡者也。

translations.literal: Li Ke held that Wu perished first because of many battles [many victories], [31] for many battles weary the people and many victories make the lord proud; with a proud lord ruling weary people, none have not perished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ke held that Wu perished first because of many battles [many victories], [31] for many battles weary the people and many victories make the lord proud; with a proud lord ruling weary people, none have not perished.

sentences.zh: 信哉言乎！

translations.literal: Trustworthy indeed are such words!
translations.idiomatic: Trustworthy indeed are such words!

sentences.zh: 高宗始以寬大得人，終以驕侈致敗，文、武之業，[32]墜于茲矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan at first won men by generosity and at the end failed by pride and extravagance; the civil and military enterprise [32] fell away at this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan at first won men by generosity and at the end failed by pride and extravagance; the civil and military enterprise [32] fell away at this.

sentences.zh: 後主生深宮之中，長婦人之手，既屬邦國殄瘁，不知稼穡艱難。

translations.literal: Houzhu was born deep in the palace and grew up in women's hands; when he came to a realm in ruin he did not know the hardship of sowing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was born deep in the palace and grew up in women's hands; when he came to a realm in ruin he did not know the hardship of sowing and reaping.

sentences.zh: 初懼阽危，屢有哀矜之詔，後稍安集，復扇淫侈之風。

translations.literal: At first he feared imminent peril and repeatedly issued edicts of pity; later, when things were somewhat settled, he again fanned the wind of lewd extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: At first he feared imminent peril and repeatedly issued edicts of pity; later, when things were somewhat settled, he again fanned the wind of lewd extravagance.

sentences.zh: 賓禮諸公，唯寄情於文酒，昵近群小，皆委之以衡軸。

translations.literal: In guest-ritual toward the lords he entrusted feeling only to letters and wine; in intimacy with petty men he entrusted them all with the pivot of power.
translations.idiomatic: In guest-ritual toward the lords he entrusted feeling only to letters and wine; in intimacy with petty men he entrusted them all with the pivot of power.

sentences.zh: 謀謨所及，遂無骨鯁之臣，權要所在，莫匪侵漁之吏。

translations.literal: Where counsel reached, there were no ministers with backbone; where power lay, there were none but officials who preyed and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Where counsel reached, there were no ministers with backbone; where power lay, there were none but officials who preyed and stripped.

sentences.zh: 政刑日紊，尸素盈朝，耽荒為長夜之飲，嬖寵同豔妻之孽，危亡弗恤，上下相蒙，眾叛親離，臨機不寤，自投於井，冀以苟生，視其以此求全，抑亦民斯下矣。

translations.literal: Government and punishments daily fell into disorder; dead wood filled the court; he indulged in drinking through the long night and favored concubines like the wickedness of a beautiful wife; peril and ruin he did not grieve; above and below deceived one another; the multitude rebelled and kin departed; facing the moment he did not awaken and threw himself into a well, hoping to live a little longer—to look on him seeking safety thus is to be beneath the people indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Government and punishments daily fell into disorder; dead wood filled the court; he indulged in drinking through the long night and favored concubines like the wickedness of a beautiful wife; peril and ruin he did not grieve; above and below deceived one another; the multitude rebelled and kin departed; facing the moment he did not awaken and threw himself into a well, hoping to live a little longer—to look on him seeking safety thus is to be beneath the people indeed.

sentences.zh: 遐觀列辟，纂武嗣興，其始也皆欲齊明日月，合德天地，高視五帝，俯協三王，然而靡不有初，克終蓋寡，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Looking far at the ranks of rulers who succeeded to martial glory, at the start they all wished to align brightness with sun and moon, join virtue with heaven and earth, look down on the Five Emperors and look up to harmonize with the Three Kings—yet scarcely none lacked a beginning while few could keep the end; what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Looking far at the ranks of rulers who succeeded to martial glory, at the start they all wished to align brightness with sun and moon, join virtue with heaven and earth, look down on the Five Emperors and look up to harmonize with the Three Kings—yet scarcely none lacked a beginning while few could keep the end; what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 並以中庸之才，懷可移之性，口存於仁義，心怵於嗜慾。

translations.literal: All alike had mediocre talent and a nature that could be shifted; the mouth stored benevolence and righteousness while the heart feared in appetite and desire.
translations.idiomatic: All alike had mediocre talent and a nature that could be shifted; the mouth stored benevolence and righteousness while the heart feared in appetite and desire.

sentences.zh: 仁義利物而道遠，嗜欲遂性而便身。

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness benefit things but the Way is far; appetite and desire follow nature and are convenient to the body.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness benefit things but the Way is far; appetite and desire follow nature and are convenient to the body.

sentences.zh: 便身不可久違，道遠難以固志。

translations.literal: Convenience to the body cannot long be left; the distant Way is hard to fix the will upon.
translations.idiomatic: Convenience to the body cannot long be left; the distant Way is hard to fix the will upon.

sentences.zh: 佞諂之倫，承顏候色，因其所好，以悅導之，若下阪以走丸，譬順流而決壅。

translations.literal: The class of flatterers, receiving the countenance and watching the color, according to what was loved guided with delight—as if going down a slope with a rolling pellet, like opening a dam along the current.
translations.idiomatic: The class of flatterers, receiving the countenance and watching the color, according to what was loved guided with delight—as if going down a slope with a rolling pellet, like opening a dam along the current.

sentences.zh: 非夫感靈辰象，降生明德，孰能遺其所樂，而以百姓為心哉？

translations.literal: Unless one was moved by the numinous and the asterisms above and heaven sent down bright virtue, who could leave what he delighted in and take the hundred surnames as his heart?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one was moved by the numinous and the asterisms above and heaven sent down bright virtue, who could leave what he delighted in and take the hundred surnames as his heart?

sentences.zh: 此所以成、康、文、景千載而罕遇，癸、辛、幽、厲靡代而不有，毒被宗社，身嬰戮辱，為天下笑，可不痛乎！

translations.literal: This is why Cheng, Kang, Wen, and Jing are rarely met in a thousand years while Gui, Xin, You, and Li are in no generation absent—poison reaching the ancestral altars, the person meeting disgrace and punishment, becoming the laughter of the realm: can it not pain one!
translations.idiomatic: This is why Cheng, Kang, Wen, and Jing are rarely met in a thousand years while Gui, Xin, You, and Li are in no generation absent—poison reaching the ancestral altars, the person meeting disgrace and punishment, becoming the laughter of the realm: can it not pain one!

sentences.zh: 古人有言，亡國之主，多有才蓺，考之梁、陳及隋，信非虛論。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying that lords of perished states often had many talents in the arts; examining Liang, Chen, and Sui, it is truly no empty remark.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had a saying that lords of perished states often had many talents in the arts; examining Liang, Chen, and Sui, it is truly no empty remark.

sentences.zh: 然則不崇教義之本，偏尚淫麗之文，徒長澆偽之風，無救亂亡之禍矣。

translations.literal: Yet if one does not honor the root of teaching and righteousness but leans to the partial in lewd and ornate letters, one only lengthens the wind of shallow falsity and cannot save the disaster of disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one does not honor the root of teaching and righteousness but leans to the partial in lewd and ornate letters, one only lengthens the wind of shallow falsity and cannot save the disaster of disorder and ruin.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：後主昔在儲宮，早標令德，及南面繼業，寔允天人之望矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Houzhu in the eastern palace early bore excellent virtue, and when he faced south and succeeded to the enterprise he truly fulfilled heaven and man's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Houzhu in the eastern palace early bore excellent virtue, and when he faced south and succeeded to the enterprise he truly fulfilled heaven and man's expectation.

sentences.zh: 至於禮樂刑政，咸遵故典，加以深弘六藝，廣辟四門，是以待詔之徒，爭趨金馬，稽古之秀，雲集石渠。

translations.literal: As for ritual, music, punishments, and government, all followed the old statutes; moreover he deeply extended the six arts and broadly opened the four gates—thus those awaiting edicts vied to reach the Golden Horse, and scholars of antiquarian learning gathered like clouds at the Stone Canal.
translations.idiomatic: As for ritual, music, punishments, and government, all followed the old statutes; moreover he deeply extended the six arts and broadly opened the four gates—thus those awaiting edicts vied to reach the Golden Horse, and scholars of antiquarian learning gathered like clouds at the Stone Canal.

sentences.zh: 且梯山航海，朝貢者往往歲至矣。

translations.literal: Moreover they climbed mountains and crossed seas; those coming to court with tribute often arrived each year.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they climbed mountains and crossed seas; those coming to court with tribute often arrived each year.

sentences.zh: 自魏正始、晉中朝以來，貴臣雖有識治者，皆以文學相處，罕關庶務，朝章大典，方參議焉，文案簿領，咸委小吏，浸以成俗，迄至于陳。

translations.literal: From Wei Zhengshi and Jin's middle court onward, though among honored ministers there were those who knew governance, all treated one another by letters and learning and rarely touched common affairs; court regulations and great statutes were for the most part discussed in council, while documents and ledgers were all entrusted to petty clerks—gradually it became custom, down to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei Zhengshi and Jin's middle court onward, though among honored ministers there were those who knew governance, all treated one another by letters and learning and rarely touched common affairs; court regulations and great statutes were for the most part discussed in council, while documents and ledgers were all entrusted to petty clerks—gradually it became custom, down to Chen.

sentences.zh: 後主因循，未遑改革，故施文慶、沈客卿之徒，專掌軍國要務，姦黠左道，以裒刻為功，自取身榮，不存國計，是以朝經墮廢，禍生鄰國。

translations.literal: Houzhu followed along and had no leisure to reform; thus Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and their kind solely held the crucial affairs of army and state—wicked and crafty in left ways, they took harsh exaction as merit, sought their own body's glory, and did not preserve the state's plan; therefore court discipline fell in ruin and disaster arose from a neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu followed along and had no leisure to reform; thus Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and their kind solely held the crucial affairs of army and state—wicked and crafty in left ways, they took harsh exaction as merit, sought their own body's glory, and did not preserve the state's plan; therefore court discipline fell in ruin and disaster arose from a neighboring state.

sentences.zh: 斯亦運鐘百六，鼎玉遷變，非唯人事不昌，蓋天意然也。

translations.literal: This too was the cycle's bell at one hundred six and the tripod jade's shift of change—not only human affairs were unprosperous; it was largely heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: This too was the cycle's bell at one hundred six and the tripod jade's shift of change—not only human affairs were unprosperous; it was largely heaven's intent.

translations.idiomatic: Again his main biography says in Zhenming year 1 he was advanced to palace attendant and does not mention special advance.

translations.idiomatic: On "there was a thing red like several dou": the Southern History annals of Houzhu read there was a thing red, large like several sheng.

sentences.zh: 按斗升二字隸書形近，書傳多訛，有訛斗為升者，有訛升為斗者。

translations.idiomatic: Note: dou and sheng in clerical script are near in form; transmitted texts often err—some err dou as sheng, some sheng as dou.

sentences.zh: 疑此脫「大」字，斗與升則未知孰是。

translations.idiomatic: This is suspected to lack large; whether dou or sheng is not yet known.
